prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
answers:
[goal] One regex in `./regex.txt` giving the last valid YYYY-MM-DD date on each log line that contains an IPv4 address.

[action] Wrote `regex.txt` (single line, one capture group so `re.findall` returns the dates):

```
^(?=.*(?<![^\W_])(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])(?:\.(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])){3}(?![^\W_])).*(?<![^\W_])([0-9]{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9])))(?![^\W_])
```

A lookahead requires an address on the line; the greedy `.*` then backtracks to the last valid date.

[result] One test run, read from the saved file with `re.MULTILINE`:
- Synthetic 4-line text returned `['2024-01-05', '2024-12-31']`, as expected. It rejected 2024-02-30, 2024-04-31, a date with a letter after it (`2024-02-29x`), a date with a digit before it (`12024-01-01`), `256.1.1.1`, `01.2.3.4`, and a line with no address.
- `server.log` gave 3 matches. I did not check these against the file line by line; only the first 5 lines were viewed.

Assumptions:
- "Letter or digit" means any Unicode letter or digit; underscore, dot and hyphen do not block. So `1.2.3.4.5` counts as containing an address, and `2024-01-05-07` contains a date.
- Any four-digit year counts, including 0000.
- A line with an address but no valid date gives nothing.
- Date and address digits are ASCII only.
